subject: Pricing & procurement path — hosted vs dedicated vs private (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Clara Ng <clara@finpulse.com>, Procurement <procurement@finpulse.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.inference.com>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing & procurement path — hosted vs dedicated vs private (recap + next steps)

Hi Clara / FinPulse team — great speaking today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary from call:
- FinPulse POC objective: integrate Redwood embeddings + chat to power customer support recommender (low-latency, <200ms token time target).
- Initial environment: hosted API for POC; target production in Q3 with expected 10M tokens/month.
- Procurement: Procurement team prefers PO / net30 for production purchases; for POC, team is open to card or centralized test account.
- Security asks: SOC2 report, encryption at rest, KMS options, and minimal data retention — Dev will validate.

Commercial & procurement questions we need to confirm (please reply inline):
1) Payment method for production: PO (Net30) or will you use credit card?
2) Marketplace interest: Would you prefer to purchase via AWS Marketplace (Redwood-managed billing) or direct invoicing from us?
3) Contract cadence: Do you have a required term for vendor commitments (12/24 months) or prefer on-demand month-to-month?
4) Paper process: Who on your side owns legal/PO sign-off and what is your internal timeline?

Proposed commercial path (from our side):
- POC: Hosted (on-demand) using card or credit for speed; we can provide $5k free trial credits for usage testing.
- Production: Two options — Dedicated reserved capacity (recommended for predictable latency & unit cost) with commits (12/24mo) OR Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads. Pricing differs by deployment and commitment level — see attached high-level proposal.

Next steps:
- Clara / procurement: confirm payment preference (PO vs card) and whether AWS Marketplace is required.
- Procurement: if PO, please share your PO template and standard invoice/billing details.
- Dev team: Dev (cc) will follow up with a short security checklist (SOC2, IAM/KMS, retention).
- We will send a short pricing proposal + SOW draft for review.

Attachments: Redwood-FinPulse-pricing-proposal-v1.pdf (high-level pricing & packaging)

Thanks — I’ll follow up once I have your inputs.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference.com | +1 415-555-0142
www.redwood.inference.com

From: Clara Ng <clara@finpulse.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finpulse.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing & procurement path — hosted vs dedicated vs private (recap + next steps)

Thanks for the clear recap, Marissa — appreciate the follow-up. Answers below: 

1) Payment method for production: We prefer PO / Net30 for any multi-month commitments. For the POC we can do either a company card or have you bill our central test card — preference is to avoid adding individual cardholders.

2) Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is preferred if pricing parity is maintained; it helps our procurement approvals and centralizes billing. Not mandatory but +1 if available.

3) Contract cadence: We try to avoid month-to-month for production. If performance/cost look good, 12-month commits are likely acceptable — we’d expect some discount for committed throughput.

4) Paper process: Legal + procurement own vendor onboarding. Typical timeline: 2–3 weeks for standard SaaS agreements; SOC2 + W9 required before PO issuance. Contact for PO/billing: billing@finpulse.com.

We’ve attached the internal PO form we use for vendors that require it. I’ll loop in procurement on the final quote after you send the pricing.

Clara
Head of Product, FinPulse
clara@finpulse.com

Subject: Re: Pricing & procurement path — hosted vs dedicated vs private (recap + next steps)

Thanks Clara — helpful answers. Quick follow-up and a proposed commercial packaging so Procurement has something to review: 

Commercial packaging (high level):
- Option A — POC / Evaluation (fast): Hosted API, on-demand pricing. No commitment. Recommended for 2–6 week technical validation. Payment: card or central test account.
- Option B — Production (predictable + lower unit cost): Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) with a 12-month commit. Discount profile: ~30% off on-demand token rates at a 12-mo committed throughput tier (~10M tokens/mo). Includes SLA and dedicated GPU pools. Invoiced via PO / Net30.
- Option C — Private (VPC / on-prem): For regulated data or where customer needs full control; pricing is subscription + infra pass-through. Typically involves an enterprise license and pricing discussed via our sales/solutions team.

Notes on Marketplace: We can list pricing via AWS Marketplace; however, marketplace billing sometimes constrains discounting and commit structures. If FinPulse needs marketplace procurement, we can provide a marketplace-friendly quote for the on-demand path and a direct PO route for committed Dedicated. We’ve seen customers do POC via marketplace (fast procurement) and switch to direct PO for committed capacity.

Requested docs we will send with the formal quote:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted)
- W9 and vendor billing information
- SOW + standard MSA (short form) for a 12-mo Dedicated commit

Next steps (action items):
- Marissa (me): finalize formal quote + SOW and send to billing@finpulse.com and procurement. Target: EOD Thu 12 Mar.
- Dev (Dev Patel): will send the security checklist and confirm retention/KMS details by tomorrow.
- Aditya (cc): will schedule a short architecture review call (30 min) if you want to validate latency/throughput targets.

If PO is the path, please confirm the contact to receive the quote (billing@finpulse.com ok) and any specific PO fields we must populate (PO number, cost center).

Thanks — attaching the high level proposal now.

Best,

Marissa Cole
